descriptiontext: The overall rate at which the price of goods and services has moved either upward or downward compared to 12 months previously.

A measure of consumer price inflation used in the government's target for inflation. The Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs (CPIH) extends the CPI to also include a measure of costs associated with owning, maintaining and living in one's home along with Council Tax.
Includes businesses trading in any capacity, including those trading at reduced capacities.
The limit on the per-unit price consumers will pay for gas and electricity between 1 October 2022 until 31 March 2023.
This is average pay adjusted for inflation.

A measure of the change in price of renting residential property from private landlords. The index is calculated using rental data collected by rent officers operating for the Valuation Office Agency, Scottish Government, Welsh Government and Northern Ireland Housing Executive (which includes data provided by propertynews.com).
This is average pay excluding bonuses.

A tax individuals pay if they buy property or land over a certain price in England and Northern Ireland. There was a temporary increase in the thresholds at which individuals start paying Stamp Duty Land Tax in 2021. Changes to Stamp Duty Land Tax reduced the amount paid for residential properties purchased between 8 July 2020 and 30 June 2021, and between 1 July 2021 and 30 September 2021, before reverting back to the pre-8 July 2021 thresholds on 1 October 2021.
The value of the goods or services sold during a particular time period.
The number of days not worked by people as a result of their involvement in a dispute at their place of work.
